newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African unions to block Swazi goods in solidarity.
newsitem.headline: S.African unions to block Swazi goods in solidarity.

text.p: South Africa's largest trade union federation said on Friday it would try to prevent the movement of goods into and out of Swaziland on Monday to support strikers in the tiny kingdom who want political reforms.
The powerful Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) said its members would also stage demonstrations on the South African side of two key border posts.

"We will go ahead with the action in Swaziland on March 3 from our side. There are effective plans to effect the blockade," Cosatu General Secretary Sam Shilowa said at a news briefing. Ordinary travellers would not be affected, he added.
A pivotal union among Cosatu's affiliates, the Transport and General Workers' Union, told reporters separately that truckers would support the protest action.
"It will be a blacking out of all movement of cargo into Swaziland. That will be the starting point," union spokesman Randall Howard said.
The three-week-old strike in the usually stable kingdom, heavily reliant on South Africa, was called by the Swaziland Federation of Trade Unions to press for democratic changes.

A 1973 royal decree vested all state powers in the monarch and banned political activity. The Swazi union leaders are to meet on Sunday to decide plans for further action possibly to coincide with Cosatu's demonstrations.

An absolute monarchy with a population of some 900,000, the mountain kingdom is heavily dependent on neighbouring South Africa which absorbs over half of Swazi exports. It is the only country in southern Africa where political parties are banned.
